review_basis: Visually inspected all sixteen original numbered WebP slides directly from GitHub, following actual layout, graphs, flows, labels and worked examples. Topic-first scenes use verified source order.
part_title: Responsible AI, Governance and AWS Accountability Tools

scenes.title: Responsible AI and Security
scenes.narration: Begin with the distinction at the top: responsible AI concerns fair, trustworthy and accountable use, while security protects the underlying information and systems. Follow the five connected lifecycle boxes. During design, identify users and potential harms. During development, choose representative data and protect sensitive information. During evaluation, test accuracy, robustness and fairness. During deployment, apply access controls and guardrails. During monitoring, look for drift, misuse and new issues. The lower row names the security triad: confidentiality prevents unauthorized access, integrity protects against tampering, and availability keeps the service usable. In the loan-application example, representative data, bias testing and a human final decision support responsible AI. Encryption, permissions and monitoring support security. A well-secured model can still be unfair, and a fair model can still be insecure: both disciplines are required.

scenes.title: Governance and Compliance
scenes.narration: This slide has four boxes connected in a loop. Policy comes first: the organization defines permitted uses, responsibilities and applicable obligations. Controls translate those written expectations into technical and operational safeguards such as access restrictions, privacy controls and model risk management. Evidence means logs, documentation and audit records that demonstrate what happened, which data was used and who approved a decision. Review assesses whether the safeguards remain effective. Notice the arrow returning to the beginning: governance must be updated as technology and regulations change. The lower hospital example uses AI to assist clinical documentation. Staff must restrict patient data access, retain suitable audit evidence and maintain human oversight. Using an AWS service does not itself guarantee compliance: the organization must determine its own requirements and verify the controls it actually operates.

scenes.title: Core Dimensions of Responsible AI
scenes.narration: Look first at the central pipeline. Data enters a model, the model generates a prediction, and a human uses that prediction to make a decision. The eight boxes around it describe different qualities this workflow needs. Fairness examines unjustified differences in outcomes; explainability helps people understand reasons; privacy and security protect assets; and transparency makes the system's purpose and limitations clear. The lower boxes add veracity and robustness for reliable outputs, governance for accountability, safety for reducing harm, and controllability for intervening when required. Follow the loan-approval example below: applicant data produces an approval likelihood, the model provides factors behind it, and a reviewer considers the explanation before deciding. A model score is evidence for a decision, not automatic authority over a person. Each dimension addresses a distinct risk and must be considered throughout the lifecycle.

scenes.title: Responsible AI: AWS Services
scenes.narration: Read the seven service columns from left to right as a comparison of capabilities, not a required single pipeline. SageMaker Data Wrangler helps prepare and analyze training data. Amazon Bedrock model evaluation examines quality and safety for supported foundation-model scenarios; Bedrock Guardrails applies configured content and usage safeguards. SageMaker Clarify supports bias analysis and explanations for configured SageMaker models, while SageMaker Model Monitor observes supported model and data quality signals after deployment. The next column shows Amazon A2I for human review, with the slide's important availability note: this service is limited to existing AWS customers. Model Cards and dashboards document purpose, results and governance information. Follow the customer-support example at the bottom, but do not assume Clarify or Model Monitor automatically evaluate Bedrock-hosted foundation models. On an exam, match the specific requirement to the applicable service and verify the deployment context.

scenes.title: AWS AI Service Cards
scenes.narration: The left card and right card describe different things. An AWS AI Service Card describes an AWS-managed AI service: its intended use, limitations and responsible-use considerations. A SageMaker Model Card documents a particular model that your team built or manages, including its data, evaluation results and known limitations. The center says choose the right card type; this is not a conversion from one document to another. The example compares consulting Amazon Rekognition's service card before use with creating a SageMaker Model Card for a separate custom model. Both help stakeholders make informed decisions, but a document cannot replace testing for fairness, security or accuracy. The exam distinction is simple: AWS service characteristics belong in a service card, while evidence about your own trained model belongs in its model card.
